scope.reason: A ceremonial observance proclamation that directs nothing.

analogs.reason: Observance proclamations of this kind are issued every year.

conflict.reason: Nothing in it conflicts with any statute or ruling.

authority.reason: Rests on the President's ordinary power to issue ceremonial proclamations.

note: Annual ceremonial observance proclamation.

scope.reason: A ceremonial month designation with no legal effect.

analogs.reason: One of many observance proclamations issued each year.

note: Ceremonial month proclamation.

scope.reason: Creates a temporary advisory commission that only recommends.

analogs.reason: Presidents routinely create advisory commissions by order, as the prior president did several times in the months before.

conflict.reason: Advisory only, no conflict with statute.

authority.reason: Cites the Federal Advisory Committee Act, the standard footing.

procedure.reason: Standard executive order form with bipartisan membership.

note: Advisory commission under FACA; the mission fixes policy principles in advance, which is a mild wrinkle, not a departure.

scope.reason: Adjusts insurance and health benefits for survivors, a modest substantive change.

analogs.reason: Follows the prior Congress's veterans benefits act in kind.

process.reason: Passed the House 417 to 0 in regular order.

note: Modest veterans' survivor benefit changes passed 417-0.

scope.reason: Gives the President $40 billion in a single emergency fund with wide discretion over its use, far beyond a usual supplemental.

analogs.reason: Earlier supplementals appropriated to named accounts; none here hands a lump sum of this size to the President.

footing.reason: An exercise of the appropriations power, with consultation and reporting conditions.

process.reason: Passed within days without the usual committee process, though 422 to 0.

note: $40 billion lump sum to a presidential fund three days after the attacks, unanimous.

scope.reason: A regular annual appropriations act with the usual riders.

analogs.reason: The same act was passed for the prior fiscal year.

footing.reason: Congress's power over the District and appropriations.

process.reason: Regular order with a conference and bipartisan majorities.

note: Annual DC appropriations act.

precedent.reason: Applies the settled Central Hudson commercial speech test.

text.reason: Constitutional question decided under existing doctrine.

procedure.reason: Ordinary certiorari review limited to the question presented.

reach.reason: Invalidates a provision of a federal statute, which is significant but done on established grounds.

note: Applies Central Hudson to strike a federal advertising ban.

precedent.reason: Extends Vernonia beyond athletes rather than breaking with it.

text.reason: Fourth Amendment reasonableness balancing under existing cases.

method.reason: Uses the special needs balancing from earlier cases.

procedure.reason: Ordinary review of a court of appeals judgment.

reach.reason: Widens permissible school drug testing, a real but incremental step.

note: Extends Vernonia's suspicionless drug testing from athletes to all extracurricular activities.

scope.reason: Changes how a child's age is fixed for visa purposes, a real but narrow substantive change.

analogs.reason: No close twin among the candidates, but narrow amendments to the immigration act are a familiar kind of law.

footing.reason: Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act under settled power.

note: Technical fix to immigration age-out rules, 416-0.

scope.reason: Ceremonial observance with no legal effect.

analogs.reason: The same observance was proclaimed the year before, and the prior president issued like proclamations.

note: Annual ceremonial month proclamation.

precedent.reason: Applies settled rules on reading tax regulations.

text.reason: Reads the statute and regulation by their terms.

reach.reason: Decides a narrow tax accounting question.

note: Routine tax regulation interpretation.

precedent.reason: Distinguishes three earlier cases rather than departing from them.

text.reason: First Amendment question resolved within existing doctrine.

method.reason: Uses familiar fraud and free speech principles.

procedure.reason: Ordinary review of a state supreme court judgment at the pleading stage.

reach.reason: Narrow holding that properly pleaded fraud claims may proceed.

note: Holds fraud suits against fundraisers survive Schaumburg, Munson and Riley; narrows a state court's broad reading without disturbing those cases.

scope.reason: Sets up data collection, a commission and national standards tied to grants, a new but modest federal program.

analogs.reason: Comparable criminal justice grant and study laws exist, though none on this subject.

footing.reason: Spending conditions and federal prison authority.

process.reason: Passed by voice vote or unanimous consent.

note: New national study, commission and standards on prison rape, passed without recorded opposition.

scope.reason: Declares a national emergency and bars most exports to one country, a serious but familiar sanctions step.

analogs.reason: Country sanctions orders under IEEPA were issued by this and the prior president.

conflict.reason: Carries out a statute rather than conflicting with one.

authority.reason: Rests on IEEPA and a statute that directed these sanctions.

procedure.reason: Follows the National Emergencies Act form.

note: New IEEPA emergency for Syria, but it implements sanctions Congress directed in the Syria Accountability Act.

scope.reason: A large emergency appropriation with transfer authority, in the usual disaster pattern.

analogs.reason: Follows earlier hurricane supplementals, including one from the prior Congress.

process.reason: Moved in days without recorded votes, which is common for disaster aid.

note: Second Katrina emergency supplemental passed within days by voice.

scope.reason: Releases $20.3 million from a standing emergency refugee fund.

analogs.reason: The prior president issued the same kind of determination several times a year.

authority.reason: Uses the statutory drawdown power as written.

note: Routine refugee fund drawdown determination.

scope.reason: Closes agencies for half a day before a holiday.

analogs.reason: The prior president issued the same order in several years.

authority.reason: Ordinary authority over the federal workforce.

note: Routine Christmas Eve half-day closing.

precedent.reason: Applies the settled rule that a waiver of sovereign immunity must be unequivocally expressed.

text.reason: Reads 'appropriate relief' narrowly in light of the immunity canon, a contestable but conventional reading.

reach.reason: Bars damages against States under one statute.

note: Applies the clear-statement rule for waivers of state sovereign immunity to RLUIPA.

scope.reason: Implements a bilateral trade agreement, a significant but standard kind of law.

analogs.reason: Tracks the implementing acts for Peru, Oman, Bahrain and CAFTA.

footing.reason: Uses the established trade promotion framework.

process.reason: Expedited trade procedures with a divided but bipartisan vote, as for earlier agreements.

note: Trade agreement implementing act under fast-track procedures, contested vote.

scope.reason: Directs programming priorities for existing broadcasters and authorizes modest funds.

analogs.reason: No close analog among the candidates, but directing existing international broadcasters is an ordinary legislative act.

footing.reason: Ordinary authorization for federally funded broadcasters.

note: Directs and funds US broadcasting to Ukraine after the Crimea events; 399-12.

scope.reason: Prohibits a named private acquisition outright, a step presidents have seldom taken.

analogs.reason: The candidates show one earlier prohibition, the 2012 Ralls order, so such blocks are rare.

authority.reason: Section 721 expressly gives the President this power and the order makes the required findings.

procedure.reason: Follows the statutory findings and form used in the earlier order.

note: Presidential order blocking a specific foreign acquisition under section 721; only one clear earlier block appears among the candidates.

scope.reason: Orders flags at half-staff for a deceased member of Congress.

analogs.reason: The same kind of proclamation was issued by this and the prior president.

note: Routine half-staff proclamation.

scope.reason: Reauthorizes and adjusts existing programs.

analogs.reason: The act has been reauthorized the same way in 2000, 2006 and 2016.

note: Periodic reauthorization of the Older Americans Act.

scope.reason: Nullifies a single agency rule on bank merger review.

analogs.reason: Earlier Congresses used the same disapproval procedure, though only occasionally.

footing.reason: Uses the statutory disapproval procedure of chapter 8 of title 5.

process.reason: Expedited procedure provided by statute, with narrow majorities in both chambers.

note: Congressional Review Act disapproval of one banking rule, near party-line.

scope.reason: Ceremonial observance with no legal effect.

analogs.reason: Proclaimed every year by this and the prior president.

note: Annual ceremonial month proclamation; the text promotes administration policy but directs nothing.

precedent.reason: Works within the James, Begay and Chambers line while giving Begay's test less weight.

text.reason: Applies an open-ended statutory clause to a new offense.

method.reason: Risk comparison as in James, with some reliance on statistics.

reach.reason: Adds one offense to the enhancement's coverage.

note: Another residual-clause case; leans on risk comparison more than Begay's test did.

precedent.reason: Applies settled rules that an agency must explain a change of position.

text.reason: Leaves the statutory question for the court of appeals.

procedure.reason: Vacates and remands without deciding the underlying question, which is ordinary.

note: Declines deference to an unexplained agency reversal and remands.

precedent.reason: Distinguishes the Rule 60(b) holding in Gonzalez rather than departing from it.

text.reason: Reads the statute against historical habeas practice.

method.reason: Conventional reliance on history and purpose of the rule and statute.

reach.reason: Narrow procedural holding on appeal timing.

note: Rule 59(e) motions are not second or successive habeas applications; distinguishes Gonzalez v. Crosby.

precedent.reason: Builds on Manuel and Heck to settle an open question.

text.reason: Section 1983 question answered by analogy to common law torts.

method.reason: Looks to the common law as of 1871, the usual approach for such claims.

procedure.reason: Ordinary certiorari review of a circuit split.

reach.reason: Eases one element of malicious prosecution claims nationwide.

note: Resolves a split on the favorable-termination element using the 1871 common law.

precedent.reason: Consistent with earlier readings of the Bankruptcy Code.

text.reason: Reads 'party in interest' by its ordinary breadth.

method.reason: Text, context and history in the usual way.

reach.reason: Narrow holding on who may be heard in a Chapter 11 case.

note: Insurer is a party in interest under section 1109(b); plain-text bankruptcy ruling.
